Class SensorData

java.lang.Object
yams.core.motorcontrollers.simulation.SensorData
public class SensorData extends Object
Sensor data class to encapsulate sensor data.

SensorData represents a single named field within a Sensor. It wraps a real-hardware supplier (e.g. a lambda reading an encoder), a default value, and an optional SimValue registered with WPILib's simulation layer so the Glass GUI can override the value during simulation without touching production code.

At runtime the getValue() method applies the following priority order:

  1. Real robot always returns the live hardware supplier value immediately.
  2. Trigger override if any registered trigger condition is currently true, the associated override value is returned and written to Glass.
  3. Glass value if a SimValue exists and no trigger fired, returns whatever Glass has set (including the default).
  4. Supplier fallback returns the supplier value if no Glass value is available.

Key fields

  • m_name the human-readable field name used as the Glass widget label.
  • m_supplier provides the real sensor reading on a physical robot.
  • m_type (SensorData.HALValueType) guards typed accessors (getAsDouble(), getAsInt(), etc.) against incorrect casts.
  • m_defaultValue the initial value published to Glass at startup.
  • m_triggerValues ordered list of (condition, value) pairs checked before the Glass value each loop.
  • m_glassValue the live SimValue registered with the parent SimDevice; empty on a real robot.

Example

// Double field backed by a real encoder
SensorData posField = new SensorData("position", encoder::getPosition, 0.0);

// Boolean field backed by a limit switch
SensorData limitField = new SensorData("atLimit", limitSwitch::get, false);

// Force a specific value in simulation when autonomous starts
posField.addSimTrigger(SensorData.convert(180.0), DriverStation::isAutonomous);

// Read the value (type-safe)
double pos = posField.getAsDouble();
